messages:
anya: Heads-up — after the 1901 deploy I'm seeing sporadic p95 tail spikes on mistral-7b for the sliding-window test set. baseline was ~45ms, now some shards hit ~120ms.
sam: ugh, when did this start? any repro script or logs?
anya: ~09:12 UTC after the kernel bump. repro with sliding-window workload (seq chunks ~512->1024, prefix reuse). Attached profiler snippet below.
perf-bot: profiler summary (batch=1, seq=1024): p50=38ms p95=118ms p99=210ms. Hot stacks: attention_kernel_selector (65%), kv_cache_write (18%), memcpy (9%).
kevin: Does kernel_selector flip to a fallback kernel under these conditions? selector rule change was part of the bump.
maria: I saw a comment earlier about rope-scaling heuristics toggling kernel paths when effective_max_pos > 1024. That might interact with cache shaping.
anya: here's the minimal config we use in the test harness:
```json
{"model":"mistral-7b","rope_scale":"auto","max_position_embeddings":"2048","kv_cache_mode":"sliding-window","batching":"adaptive_small","adaptive_threshold":0.6}
```
sam: interesting — adaptive_threshold 0.6 means small batches will prefer low-latency kernels but the selector also considers kv_cache_hit_ratio.
kevin: quick grep in kernel_selector: if (rope_scaled && seq > 1024 && kv_hit < 0.7) choose kernel_v2_rope_window; else choose kernel_v1_contig. That explains flips mid-run when cache warms.
maria: flips are bad because kv cache layout changes (tile layout vs contig) and we do an extra memcpy/transform during flip, which explains memcpy in profiler.
anya: repro timeline from logs:
- 09:11:58 request stream starts, seq growth
- 09:12:03 kernel_selector chooses v1
- 09:12:08 cache hit ratio dips to 0.62 -> selector flips to v2
- 09:12:08 runtime issues kernel switch hook -> do cache reformat
- 09:12:08..09:12:10 request experiences ~80ms extra latency spike

sam: can we make the selector hold stable for active requests? like only allow kernel flips between requests or when no outstanding tokens?
kevin: We already have a scheme but it's per-worker; this shows we allow flip while request pending. Quick patch idea: block flips while any inflight token_count > 0 or when sliding-window active.
maria: Another mitigation: add hysteresis on kv_hit ratio (e.g., require <0.6 for N consecutive checks) and prefer kernels that avoid expensive reformat path.
anya: I ran a quick experiment forcing kernel_v1 (old path) and p95 went back to 47ms. Forcing v2 gives 115ms. So v2 path is slower for this workload.
perf-bot: microbench: kernel_v1 throughput 201 toks/s latency 36ms; kernel_v2 throughput 187 toks/s latency 98ms. KV reformat adds ~70ms when triggered.
sam: two-pronged plan: (1) hotfix to disable in-flight kernel flips + hysteresis; (2) deeper followup to optimize v2 path or improve reformat path.
kevin: I'll draft the hotfix now. small change in kernel_selector: add inflight_guard && kv_hysteresis counter. Should be non-disruptive.
maria: I'll profile the reformat path — suspect extra mem copies and non-vectorized loop for the tile->contig conversion. Might be able to do an inplace transform or build a lightweight view.
anya: owners: kevin hotfix, maria profile and PR for reformat perf, sam coordinate canary. I'll run a canary cluster with hotfix toggled.
runtime-bot: deploy-plan created: canary=eng-runtime-canary1, rollout=10% -> 50% -> 100% if p95<60ms after 30m.
sam: thanks — let's try to avoid kernel churn next deploy. @kevin @maria ping me when you push PRs.
kevin: will do. pushing hotfix branch 'no-inflight-flips' in ~20m.
maria: prepping perf trace now, will share flamegraphs.
anya: cool. if anyone hits repro, add logs: kernel_choice, kv_hit_ratio, inflight_tokens, and whether reformat happened. that will help confirm.
sam: ack. good triage, team. :thumbsup:
